next_question: Can a third recipe variant (e.g., meta-analytic combination of canonical and weighted, or a new structural recipe) break the 2-recipe dominance degeneracy and make the OECD/COINr framework informative for MIXED outcome handling — and does this reformulated decision rule survive on full-DOM data after the runtime lane removes the locatableSample cap?
why_next: The OECD/COINr framework is designed for 3+ alternatives. With exactly 2 recipes, dominance is necessarily binary (0%/100%), making C2_DOMINANCE_INFORMATIVE construct-impossible (audit V2). The frozen decision_rule has no bucket for the observed C-pattern. Three forward paths exist: (1) add a third recipe to break degeneracy — highest information gain because it directly tests whether OECD framework becomes informative; (2) reformulate C2 for 2-recipe comparisons (density ratio, ranking reversal rate); (3) await full-DOM data where recipe choice may resolve differently. All paths still require the runtime lane to remove the locatableSample cap at measure_fullpage_yield.py:89 for empirical validation. The third-recipe path is orthogonal to the full-DOM path and can proceed independently.

do_not_assume: Do NOT use OECD/COINr framework with only 2 recipes to justify recipe choice — dominance is necessarily degenerate (0%/100%) by construction, not by scientific finding.
Do NOT assume the 84.7x cross-recipe density ratio is a validated scientific result — it is observed on truncated-first-20 data (locatable_sample cap 20) and may change with full DOM enumeration.

Do NOT assume the OECD/COINr framework has been validated for SPIDER's density metric — this experiment demonstrated it is NOT informative in the 2-recipe setting (construct failure, not empirical validation).
Do NOT assume SPIDER-to-field applicability mappings are established results — they are interpretive analogies bounded by audit findings.
Do NOT assume the non-systematic literature search captured all relevant prior art — a formal systematic review may yield additional methods.
Do NOT assume the FALSIFIED conclusion generalizes to full-DOM — truncated-first-20 is a non-representative slice.
Do NOT assume the per-iteration recipe is universally canonical beyond this experiment's scope.
Do NOT assume the density metric is entirely useless — ordering-based discrimination is definition-sensitive and recipe-sensitive, not that density values are uninformative.
Do NOT assume recipe choice is a nuisance parameter — it is a MATERIAL determinant of the scientific conclusion.
Do NOT assume C-MEAS-VALID status changed from this experiment — it remains EXPERIMENTAL; this experiment attempted framework operationalization, not empirical measurement validation.
Do NOT assume quantitative parent values are reliable — deviations exceed frozen thresholds.
Do NOT assume the MIXED outcome decision rule is resolved — it remains open pending either third-recipe operationalization or full-DOM empirical validation.
